newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Foods favours Avonmore merger.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Foods favours Avonmore merger.

text.p: The board of Waterford Foods Plc and Waterford Co-operative, on Friday voted in favour of a proposed merger with Avonmore Foods Plc.
Waterford said in a statement that 83 percent of those attending a special meeting held in the southern country of Waterford, voted yes to a merger with Avonmore.
Earlier 97.6 percent of Avonmore Creameries members, who own 63.9 percent of Avonmore Foods Plc, voted in favour of the merger, at a meeting held simultaneously in the midlands town of Kilkenny.
"This is indeed an historic day for farmers of the south east," Waterford Co-operative chairman John Downey said in a statement. "It augers well for the future of the dairy industry."
To succeed the merger has to be approved by 75 percent of the farmers who attend two consecutive extraordinary general meetings.
The second meeting is scheduled for July 25 to ratify today's outcome.
If the merger succeeds the turnover for the combined entity will exceed 2.5 billion Irish pounds with pre-tax profits of 71.5 million.
This will create the largest dairy company in Britain and Ireland and the fourth largest milk processor in the world.
This is the second time in six years that Avonmore has attempted to merge with Waterford after a similar attempt in 1991 failed.
